newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreign-favoured shares rise on Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Foreign-favoured shares rise on Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Trading on the Nairobi Stock Exchange was mixed on Thursday with most key issues easing marginally while shares supported by foreign demand edged up.

The NSE 20-share index was down 41.85 points to close at 3397.24. Turnover was posted at 13.1 million shillings traded on 353,600 shares compared to 49.8 million shillings on 2,940,005 shares on Wednesday.
Lonrho Motors shed 9.50 to close at 49 while Total Kenya closed at 65 from 70. British American Tobacco (BAT) Kenya eased to 61 from 62.50.
"Foreigners have a very big appetite for Kenya Commercial Bank," a bourse official said. They bought the bank at 102 unchanged.
A senior broker said despite the market dip, investors were buying those shares they believed were strong on fundamentals and undervalued.
Kenya Power & Lighting was unchanged at 170 while Nation Printers & Publishers edged up to 109 from 103.
Standard Chartered Bank closed at 46.75 from 46 while Marshalls (E.A) moved up to 71.50 from 66. Cooper Motors Corporation (CMC) Holdings closed at 81.50 from 78.50.
Sasini Tea & Coffee traded at 78 from 77 while Rea Vipingo was unchanged at 9.
The Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond traded 400,000 shillings at 104.7440 percent unchanged.
